Can you get us a recommended fleet plan and a ballpark price by EOW? We may also want Redwood to provision a short proof-of-concept pool for load testing.

Appreciate it — happy to jump on a call.

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Alaire Ops <ops@alaire.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>

Subject: RE: Sizing request: dedicated GPUs for LLM inferencing (13B / 70B) — initial technical assessment

Hi all — I took a first pass based on the traffic numbers and model choices. Below is a concise technical summary and a recommended starting pool. I'll attach a detailed breakout (spreadsheet + memory diagrams) to the shared drive.

High-level assumptions I used:
- Tokenization: average tokens per call (prompt+reply) ~120 tokens.
- Peak requests convert to concurrent inflight tokens depending on per-request latency; I assumed 200–400ms p90 for 13B and 600ms for 70B for SLO planning.
- No heavy tooling/function-calls; mostly standard autoregressive generation with streaming.

Model memory and KV-cache notes (ballpark numbers):
- Llama2-13B (FP16): parameter storage ~13B * 2 bytes ≈ 26 GB. Runtime overhead (workspace, activations) + CUDA buffers ≈ 6–10 GB. So base footprint ≈ 34–36 GB on-host.
- KV cache: scales with context length and #heads/hidden-dim. Practical numbers:
  • 8k context (13B): expect ~5–8 GB for KV cache (fp16 storage).
  • 32k bursts (13B): ~20–24 GB for KV cache.
- Combined (13B, 32k): total host memory ~56–60 GB (model + kv + temp). That means 13B with 32k context is tight for single 48 GB GPUs — prefer 80 GB-class GPUs or multi-GPU partitioning.

- 70B model (FP16): parameters ~70B * 2 bytes ≈ 140 GB. Runtime overhead + kv cache for 32k context will push total >160–170 GB. This cannot fit on a single GPU unless heavily quantized and then still usually requires model/shard across multiple 80GB-class GPUs.

Impact of quantization:
- Weight quantization (4-bit / q4 / int8) reduces parameter memory by ~2.5–3.5x depending on scheme and accuracy target. So a 70B in q4 could have effective param storage ~40–55 GB.
- Important caveat: KV cache and activations are usually kept in FP16 (or FP32 for some kernels) to preserve numeric stability — quantizing weights helps model parameter memory but does not proportionally reduce KV cache. In other words: quantization helps fit parameters but KV cache still dominates for long contexts.
- There are experimental KV-cache compression tricks (e.g., quantizing KV to 8-bit or downcasting) that can yield ~1.3–1.6x reduction in KV size with small quality tradeoffs; treat as optional optimization, not primary strategy.

Throughput and GPU sizing (recommended starting pools):
- 13B (primary path, mostly 8k): 1 x A100-80GB or H100-80GB can host ~1–2 realtime low-latency worker processes with headroom for 32k bursts if you enable KV caching per-client and avoid worst-case concurrency. For 60 RPS peak (assuming average per-request latency ~250ms), you need ~15 concurrent in-flight requests. With batching and concurrency tuning we can get ~6–8 RPS per GPU for low latency; conservatively plan 3–4 GPUs for redundancy and smoothing (pool of 4 x 80GB).
- 70B (32k): practical deployment is 4-way model-sharded across 4 x 80GB GPUs (A100/H100). With q4 quantization you can sometimes run 2-way sharding on 80GB, but this is less resilient. For 60 RPS non-batched at 600ms p90 you'd want at least 6–8 shards (i.e., multiple model replicas) to get target throughput; recommend starting with 8 x 80GB GPUs for the 70B fleet (2 replicas of 4-way shards) and scale based on perf testing.

Operational recommendations and levers:
- Use automatic KV cache prefixing (session caching) for customers with repeated prompts — this cuts effective KV storage pressure and reduces per-request compute.
- Route heavy 32k requests to dedicated nodes with larger GPUs to avoid polluting 13B pool.
- Enable quantized model variants as fallback (e.g., fp16 replica and q4 replica) with automated fallback when capacity is constrained.

Ballpark cost / procurement notes (very rough):
- 4 x 80GB GPUs (13B pool) + infra/hosting premium ≈ monthly committed cost X (we'll put numbers in the spreadsheet).
- 8 x 80GB GPUs (70B pool) + redundancy ≈ monthly committed cost Y.

Next steps / asks from Alaire:
1) Confirm: percent of requests that will hit 32k context for 13B (you said ~1% — confirm).
2) Confirm region preference and whether you need multi-region failover.
3) If possible, provide a token-length histogram (prompt + reply) for one representative day — that will let us refine KV sizing.

I'll upload the detailed workbook (20260302-alaire-dedicated-sizing.xlsx) and a short PDF with memory diagrams. We can iterate after Claire shares exact token distribution. Happy to jump on a sizing call.

— Aditya
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Aditya — this aligns with our internal runbooks. A few operational items to call out for procurement & onboarding: 

- Autoscaling policy: recommend reserved baseline capacity (enough to meet steady-state) + burstable pool for peak. For Alaire's numbers: reserve capacity equal to steady 12 RPS (saves cost), add burst pool for the 60 RPS peaks.
- Fallbacks & rollout: gate the 70B rollout behind a canary (1 replica) + automatic fallback to 13B q4 when latency or queueing increases.
- SLA/maintenance windows: if they plan 24/7 low latency, we recommend two AZs in region and staggered maintenance for predictable failover.
- Security / compliance: we'll need SOC2 evidence and a brief of encryption key handling for Private/Dedicated options — I'll attach our evidence packet separately if procurement requests it.

I updated the spreadsheet with operational cost levers and a proposed rollout timeline. See attached: 20260303-gpu-memory-breakdown.pdf.

Claire —

Thanks — attaching our synthesis. Summary highlights: 
- 13B pool recommendation: start with 4 x 80GB workers (A100/H100), enable session KV caching, quantized fallback option.
- 70B pool recommendation: start with 8 x 80GB GPUs (two 4-way replicas) using q4 for parameter memory reduction; plan for model-sharded replicas behind the router.
- KV-cache caveat: long-context workloads (32k) drive memory more than parameter size; quantization mainly helps parameter memory. Consider prefix caching and rate-limiting very long contexts to control costs.

Attached: 20260302-alaire-dedicated-sizing.xlsx (detailed numbers) and 20260303-gpu-memory-breakdown.pdf.
